title: A Vaccine for Epstein-Barr Virus: Gary Nabel on The Long Run - TimmermanReport.com
gist: Podcast episode intro: Gary Nabel (ex-Sanofi CSO, ex-NIH), now CEO of ModeX Therapeutics, is in clinical trials with a Merck-partnered vaccine against Epstein-Barr Virus — a virus with no approved vaccine that is implicated in several cancers, multiple sclerosis, and autoimmune disease — built on a multi-specific biologics platform also aimed at cancer and COVID-19.

insights.claim: ModeX Therapeutics, partnered with Merck, has a vaccine candidate against Epstein-Barr Virus in clinical trials, targeting a virus for which no vaccine currently exists.
insights.speaker: @ldtimmerman
insights.so_what: First-mover position in an unaddressed vaccine market with a big-pharma partner; watch clinical readouts for validation of the multi-specific platform.
insights.quote: There is no vaccine against the virus, and the ModeX candidate still has a long way to go.
insights.locator: The initial application of this technology

insights.claim: EBV, which lies dormant in most adults, can reactivate later in life and is implicated as a cause of several cancers, multiple sclerosis, and autoimmune diseases — so an EBV vaccine could theoretically prevent a broad set of debilitating chronic diseases, far beyond mononucleosis.
insights.speaker: @ldtimmerman
insights.so_what: The addressable value of an EBV vaccine scales with the strengthening EBV-MS/cancer causality evidence — upside optionality well beyond an anti-mono shot.
insights.quote: EBV is implicated as a culprit in several types of cancer, multiple sclerosis, and autoimmune diseases.
insights.locator: This virus is known to cause

insights.claim: ModeX's multi-specific biologics platform is being applied across three modalities — vaccines (EBV), immune-stimulating cancer treatments, and treating or preventing COVID-19 — giving the company multiple shots on goal from one technology toolkit.
insights.speaker: @ldtimmerman
insights.so_what: Platform breadth diversifies single-asset risk; success in EBV would de-risk the cancer and infectious-disease applications of the same toolkit.
insights.quote: ModeX is using the same technology toolkit to spur an immune response against cancer and to treat or prevent COVID-19.

insights.claim: The EBV vaccine opportunity emerged from the convergence of two trends: deeper understanding of EBV infection biology and expanding capabilities in antibody engineering — a template for how new vaccine targets become tractable.
insights.speaker: @ldtimmerman
insights.so_what: Screen for other pathogens where biology insight plus engineering toolkits are converging — that intersection is where new vaccine franchises get created.
insights.quote: deeper understanding of the biology of EBV infections, and the expanding capabilities in the antibody engineering toolkit, have led us to this point of possibility

insights.claim: ModeX was founded in 2020 by Gary Nabel, building directly on work begun at Sanofi where he was chief scientific officer, after a career as a virologist with senior scientific positions at the NIH — pedigree that lends credibility to the platform and helps explain the Merck partnership.
insights.speaker: @ldtimmerman
insights.so_what: Pharma-CSO-turned-founder with NIH roots is a quality signal in biotech diligence; the Sanofi provenance suggests the platform is mature, not de novo startup science.
insights.locator: Gary is the CEO of Weston
